questions.explanation:
The vapour pressure plot for liquid versus mole fraction of is represented as :



(i) Point A on plot represents vapour pressure due to pure L (its mole fraction being 1) and point represents vapour pressure due to pure . Point represents vapour pressure due to pure liquid as mole fraction of liquid becomes maximum.

(ii) The dotted line represents increase in the vapour of the pure liquid with increase in its concentration. Here, pure liquid follows Raoult's law.

(iii) The red coloured curve on above the dotted line shows positive deviation shown by liquid M from the Raoult's law.

(a) Since mole fraction of pure liquid is max at point ; hence, this point represents vapour pressure due to pure liquid . There is no curve corresponding to pure liquid component L; hence, whether liquid L obey' Raoult's law or not cannot be predicted.

Option (A) is incorrect.

(b) Since mole fraction of liquid L is maximum at point B, which also corresponds to the maximum vapour pressure at point ; hence, point represents the vapour pressure of pure liquid .

Option (B) is correct.

(c) At point Z, the molefraction of liquid component and lies above the vapour pressure curve for pure L (The dotted line). Therefore, the mixture obeys positive deviation from the Raoult's law. This means intermolecular force of attraction are lower between and L; then that between M-M and L-L.

Option (D) is correct.
